q: What is the correct full form of VDU?
explain: VDU stands for Visual Display Unit and is commonly used as another term for a monitor. 'Vast Display Unit' is incorrect.

q: A computer monitor is classified as:
explain: A monitor shows text, pictures, graphics and video, so it is an output device.

q: How is the size of a monitor screen measured?
explain: Screen size is the diagonal of the viewable screen, usually in inches. It excludes the bezel and stand.

q: A '24-inch monitor' refers to the nominal:
explain: The 24 inches is the nominal diagonal of the viewable screen, not its width or height.

q: For a rectangular screen, the diagonal can be found using which relationship?
explain: The diagonal follows the Pythagorean theorem: the square root of (width² + height²).

q: Which of the following is the unit commonly used for screen size?
explain: Screen size is quoted in inches. Pixels measure resolution, hertz refresh rate and nits luminance.

q: What does a resolution of 1920 x 1080 mean?
explain: Resolution is horizontal pixels x vertical pixels, so 1920 x 1080 is a pixel count, not a size in inches.

q: Which resolution is called Full HD?
explain: Full HD (1080p) is 1920 x 1080. 2048 x 1080 is DCI 2K cinema, and 1280 x 720 is HD.

q: Which resolution is QHD (WQHD / 1440p)?
explain: QHD is 2560 x 1440, which is higher than Full HD.

q: How many times as many pixels does a consumer 4K UHD display (3840 x 2160) have compared with Full HD?
explain: 3840 x 2160 is 8,294,400 pixels, exactly four times Full HD (2,073,600).

q: Which of the following is the correct resolution of 8K UHD?
explain: 8K UHD is 7680 x 4320. 3840 x 2160 is 4K UHD.

q: VGA is commonly quoted as which legacy resolution?
explain: The commonly cited legacy VGA format is 640 x 480, although it is not a universal definition.

q: The word 'pixel' is derived from:
explain: A pixel is a 'picture element', the smallest individual element of a digital image.

q: Monitors create colours using which model?
explain: Monitors combine red, green and blue light, which is an additive colour model. CMYK is used by colour printing.

q: Which colour depth is known as True Color?
explain: 24-bit RGB (8 bits per channel) gives about 16.7 million colours and is called True Color.

q: How many colours are possible with a 16-bit total colour depth (High Color)?
explain: 2 to the power 16 is 65,536 colours, commonly called High Color.

q: A display uses 8 bits per RGB channel. How many colours can it show?
explain: 8 bits per channel is 24 bits in total: 256 x 256 x 256, about 16.7 million colours. Only 8 bits in total would give 256.

q: Pixel density is measured in:
explain: PPI means pixels per inch. Hz is refresh rate, ms is response time and nits is luminance.

q: The refresh rate of a monitor is expressed in:
explain: Refresh rate is the number of image updates per second, measured in hertz. A 60 Hz display refreshes 60 times each second.

q: Pixel response time is usually measured in:
explain: Response time is how long a pixel transition takes, commonly in milliseconds. It is different from refresh rate.

q: At the same screen size, a higher native resolution generally gives:
explain: More pixels in the same area raise the PPI, which can give sharper detail.

q: Nits are a unit used to measure a monitor's:
explain: One nit equals one candela per square metre (cd/m²) and measures luminance. It is not an abbreviation for night visibility.

q: Which of the following is an Indian monitor brand mentioned in the book?
explain: Zebronics is the Indian brand listed; BenQ, Acer and Lenovo are not Indian brands.

q: Which display technology uses electron guns to direct electron beams onto a phosphor-coated screen?
explain: A CRT (Cathode Ray Tube) uses electron guns. It is bulky and is not a flat-panel display.

q: A conventional 'LED monitor' is best described as:
options: An LCD panel lit by LED backlights
explain: In an LED monitor the picture is still formed by liquid crystals; LEDs only act as the backlight.

q: CCFL, the backlight used in older LCD monitors, stands for:
explain: CCFL is the Cold Cathode Fluorescent Lamp. LED backlights replaced it in most modern LCDs.

q: TFT LCD is known as which type of display?
explain: In a TFT (Thin-Film Transistor) LCD, transistors control the pixels or subpixels, which makes it an active-matrix display.

q: Which statement about liquid crystals in an LCD is correct?
options: They control the passage of light
explain: Liquid crystals only control how light passes through; they do not produce light themselves. A backlight is needed.

q: Which display technology works by exciting small gas-filled cells into ionised gas so that phosphors glow?
explain: Plasma displays use ionised gas; ultraviolet radiation then excites phosphors to give visible light.

q: A conventional QLED display is based on:
options: An LED-backlit LCD enhanced with quantum dots
explain: QLED is an LED-backlit LCD with quantum dots for better colour. OLED, not QLED, uses organic emitters.

q: Which technology has organic elements that produce light directly, so individual pixels can switch off for deep blacks?
explain: OLED (Organic Light-Emitting Diode) pixels emit their own light and can turn off completely, giving deep blacks and high contrast.

q: Which statement about Mini-LED and MicroLED is correct?
options: Mini-LED is an LCD backlight, while MicroLED uses self-emitting inorganic LEDs
MicroLED is an LCD backlight, while Mini-LED is self-emitting
Both use liquid crystals as the light source
explain: Mini-LED uses smaller LEDs behind an LCD, so its pixels are not self-emissive. MicroLED uses microscopic inorganic LEDs that emit their own light.

q: Which of the following generates its own light directly and is NOT an OLED?
explain: MicroLED (and plasma) also produce light directly, so self-emission is not exclusive to OLED. The other options still depend on a backlight.

q: Which is the oldest display technology among CRT, LCD, plasma and OLED?
explain: CRT is the oldest of the listed technologies and is bulky and deep-bodied.

q: Which statement is the most accurate about power consumption of displays?
options: MicroLED always uses the least power
OLED always uses the least power
It depends on size, brightness, content and the specific model
CRT always uses the least power
explain: Power use cannot be decided by technology name alone; compare equal size, brightness, content and model specifications.

q: Which sequence matches the simplified exam order of monitor types?
explain: The study sequence is CRT, LCD, LED-backlit LCD, OLED. It is a broad guide, not an exact invention timeline.

q: Which statement about colour depth is correct?
options: 24-bit RGB gives 2²⁴ colours, called True Color
explain: 24-bit RGB gives 2²⁴ (about 16.7 million) colours and is called True Color. 8 bits total gives only 256, and 16 bits gives 65,536.
